binders: A measurable space Ω and a probability measure μ on it.
A natural-indexed sequence of real-valued random variables X.
Real parameters m and σ with σ > 0.
hypotheses: The family X is mutually independent under μ.
Every Xᵢ has the same distribution as X₀.
The expectation of X₀ is m and its variance is σ².
conclusions: As N tends to infinity, the probability that the normalized centered sum of the first N+1 variables lies in [t,infinity) converges to the standard-normal right-tail probability.
The limiting value is the displayed Gaussian-density integral over [t,infinity), converted to an extended nonnegative real.
mathematical_definitions: The normalized centered n-term sum is the sum of Xᵢ-m over i<n scaled by the reciprocal of σ√n.
Each law is the pushforward of μ under that normalized sum.
Set.Ici t is the closed upper ray [t,infinity).
The standard-normal tail is (1/√(2π)) times the integral of exp(-x²/2) over that ray.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any square-integrable iid real sequence with mean m and positive standard deviation σ, the probability that its standardized centered partial sum exceeds any fixed threshold converges to the corresponding standard-normal upper-tail probability.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion concerns closed upper-ray probabilities rather than an abstract weak-convergence predicate.
The sample size is N+1, so the normalization is never evaluated at zero terms.
The Gaussian integral is converted with ENNReal.ofReal; its integrand and integral are nonnegative.
Square integrability supplies measurability and finite second moments.
Positive σ and variance σ² exclude the degenerate zero-variance case.
ambiguities: The almost-everywhere details inside IdentDistrib and iIndepFun are measure-theoretic infrastructure.
No convergence rate or finite-sample error bound is asserted.
